last.verdict: MetLife posted its best quarterly profit per share ever, but a 49% jump in volatile investment income did much of the lifting.

takeaways.label: Record earnings
takeaways.text: Adjusted earnings per share excluding one-time items rose 22% to $2.85, a company record. Return on equity was 19.6%, up from 16.7% a year earlier.

takeaways.label: Investment income boost
takeaways.text: Variable investment income, the lumpy returns from private-equity-type holdings, rose 49% to $720 million. It drove much of the profit growth, so the pace may not repeat.

takeaways.label: Growth everywhere
takeaways.text: Premiums and fees excluding large pension deals rose 8% to $13.5 billion, with growth in all six segments. Group Benefits profit rose 14% on better claims results.

takeaways.label: Soft spots
takeaways.text: Latin America profit excluding one-time items fell 5% at constant exchange rates. Asia sales dropped 6% against a strong prior-year quarter.

history.verdict: Investors cheered a clear profit beat driven by better insurance claims results.

reasons.label: Earnings beat
reasons.text: Adjusted earnings of $2.43 per share topped analyst estimates of about $2.29.

reasons.label: Better claims results
reasons.text: Group Benefits profit jumped 25% to $503 million on favorable underwriting and volume growth.

reasons.label: Broad growth, high returns
reasons.text: Every segment grew; return on equity hit 17% for a second straight quarter.
